h: Plan a Proper Toon Night Around It
p: A good games night is all about the planning, especially with a big group. Book ahead, particularly for Fridays, Saturdays and the run-up to Christmas, and agree a meeting time that's a little before your slot so nobody's still on the Metro when the first round starts. If your crew is the competitive type, split into balanced teams and decide on a forfeit for the losers before anyone's had a drink.

Newcastle's Metro makes getting around easy, and it'll also take you out to the coast. Tynemouth, at the mouth of the Tyne, has a priory and castle on the headland, a lovely beach and a weekend market in the old station, so it's ideal for a breezy morning before a night of games in town.

Fancy a bit more culture? The Ouseburn Valley, just east of the city centre, is full of creative spaces, pubs and music venues, while the Laing Art Gallery in the centre hosts a range of exhibitions. Football fans can't miss St James' Park, which looms over the city centre from its hilltop spot.

For a classic photo, the Angel of the North, Antony Gormley's huge steel sculpture, stands on a hill in Gateshead and is worth a quick stop if you're driving in from the south. It's one of the most recognisable landmarks in the North East.
